references.text: Connects the Lord's judgment over the ends of the earth and His case against the nations, where Jeremiah elaborates on the fate of the wicked as warned in 1 Samuel.
Shares a motif concerning the Lord's vengeance against 'adversaries' and God's character as a jealous judge who upholds justice.
Connects the Lord's coming to judge the earth with righteousness, where Psalm 96:13 elaborates on the nature of judgment as an expression of God's faithfulness.
Identical thematic parallel with Psalm 96:13 regarding the Lord's judgment over the earth, confirming God's righteous nature in 1 Samuel.
Uses the specific image 'to lift up a horn' to show God's sovereignty, either as blessing for His anointed or judgment against enemies.
Connects the Lord's judgment as a force of nature (thunder/storm) that strikes the wicked and adversaries.
Contrast between God's anointed king who receives strength (1 Sam) and the self-exalted adversary who meets judgment (Daniel).
